About Williams-Sonoma, Inc.
  
  
Founded in 1956 and headquartered in San Francisco, California, Williams-Sonoma, Inc. is a Fortune 500, digital first, multi-channel specialty retailer. Our company vision is to own the home, and the places where our customers work, stay, and play. We bring the latest home furnishing trends to life for customers through the individual lenses of our ten distinct brands, each serving different life stages and rooms of the home and beyond. Our brands include Williams Sonoma, Williams Sonoma Home, Pottery Barn, Pottery Barn Kids, Pottery Barn Teen, West Elm, Rejuvenation, Mark & Graham, GreenRow, and Dormify. We are committed to sustainability, continuously working to protect our planet, while building an open and collaborative culture across our organization.
  
  
With more than 500 retail stores globally and multiple international franchise operations, technology is a core driver of our business strategy. We build and operate in-house platforms powering e-commerce, supply chain, merchandising, analytics, and customer experience ecosystems worldwide.
  
  
The Logistics Technology team at Williams-Sonoma, Inc. builds and supports the platforms that move product across our supply chain — from distribution center operations and warehouse management to transportation and delivery for brands including Williams Sonoma, Pottery Barn, West Elm, and Rejuvenation. We partner closely with Supply Chain, Distribution Center operations, and third-party vendors to deliver scalable microservices that keep fulfillment fast, accurate, and cost-effective. It is a hands-on, high-ownership team where engineers work end to end — designing systems, integrating with WMS and TMS platforms, and applying automation and AI to improve how our distribution network runs every day.

The Staff Software Engineer will be responsible for leading the design, development, and delivery of enterprise-grade, scalable microservices applications supporting Logistics and Warehouse Management Systems. This role requires strong technical leadership, hands-on development expertise, and close collaboration with cross-functional business and technology teams, including third-party vendors such as Manhattan Associates.

* Lead integrations across Warehouse Management, Transportation Management, Slotting, and Labor Management systems and Distribution Center operations.
* Identify and deliver AI and automation opportunities that improve Logistics operations, production support, and business-user productivity.
* Drive Agile delivery and mentor engineers to raise the bar across the team.
* Guide teams, drive execution, and deliver measurable business value.

* Manhattan WMOS

* Own application health in production — monitoring, alerting, incident triage, and root-cause resolution.
* Lead integrations across Warehouse Management, Transportation Management, Slotting, and Labor Management systems and Distribution Center operations.
* Partner with business stakeholders and third-party vendors such as Manhattan Associates to translate logistics requirements into scalable technical solutions.
* Identify and deliver AI and automation opportunities that improve Logistics operations, production support, and business-user productivity.
* Drive Agile delivery — sprint planning, estimation, and delivery tracking — and mentor engineers to raise the bar across the team.

**Qualifications**

* 10+ years of software engineering experience, including at least 3 years as a Java Lead.
* Proven track record delivering enterprise-scale microservices applications in a retail, supply chain, or logistics environment.
* Experience delivering in Agile environments using Jira for sprint planning, estimation, and delivery tracking.

* Hands-on experience integrating with Manhattan WMOS, Transportation Management Systems, Manhattan Slotting, and Labor Management systems.
* Experience leading third-party vendor integrations, integration platforms, and enterprise web services.

title: Senior Technical Support Consultant
description:
**About Armor Defense Inc**
At Armor, we are committed to making a meaningful difference in securing cyberspace. Our vision is to be the trusted protector and de facto standard that cloud-centric customers entrust with their risk. We strive to continuously evolve to be the best partner of choice, breaking norms and tirelessly innovating to stay ahead of evolving cyber threats and reshaping how we deliver customer outcomes. We are passionate about making a positive impact in the world, and we’re looking for a highly skilled and experienced talent to join our dynamic team.
  
  
Armor has unique offerings to the market so customers can a) understand their risk b) leverage Armor to co-manage their risk or c) completely outsource their risk to Armor.
  
  
Learn more at: https://www.armor.com
  
  
**Summary**
The Technical Program Manager owns Armor’s problem-management program and the analytical work that drives down the volume of issues customers experience. This is a program and analysis role, not a day-to-day ticket-resolution role: rather than working individual customer tickets, the Technical Program Manager digs into the data behind them to find the systemic problems that generate recurring work, and drives those to permanent resolution or a clear, repeatable framework. That work is grounded in understanding how data flows into Armor’s systems—the connectors, APIs, and ingestion pipelines behind platforms such as Microsoft Sentinel and Microsoft Defender—so root causes and data-quality issues can be identified, not guessed. The role partners closely with Engineering, SRE, and support delivery teams and thinks in terms of measurable, repeatable outcomes rather than one-off fixes—an approach that matters deeply for a cybersecurity company where recurring problems carry real customer risk. Based in Pune, India, the role works primarily on India business hours and carries the flexibility to overlap with US Central hours as needed to collaborate with Armor’s Dallas-based Engineering, SRE, and delivery teams. It reports to and takes strategic direction from the Head of Global Support.
  
  
**Essential Duties And Responsibilities**

* Analyze incident and ticket data to identify the systemic drivers of ticket volume, and target measurable reductions in recurring work and customer-impacting incidents.
* Investigate how data flows into Armor’s systems—connectors, APIs, and ingestion pipelines from Microsoft Sentinel, Microsoft Defender, Qualys/VMDR, log/SIEM sources, and Azure and cloud telemetry—to surface data-quality issues and the root causes behind recurring problems.
* Work through ambiguity: develop hypotheses about recurring and systemic problems, validate root cause with data, and ensure problems are genuinely understood before solutions are pursued.
* Consolidate recurring incidents and service requests into managed problem records and drive them to permanent resolution or a clear, repeatable framework—without taking over day-to-day ticket execution, which is owned by dedicated delivery teams.
* Build the queries, dashboards, and reports that surface trends and quantify customer and business impact (e.g., KQL over Sentinel/Defender, SQL, Power BI, and Jira reporting).
* Lead root cause analysis (RCA) for major and recurring problems; document root causes, workarounds, and known errors so delivery teams resolve recurrences consistently.
* Partner with Engineering, SRE, and delivery teams to land systemic fixes, and coordinate permanent fixes that require change through Armor’s change process.
* Define and report the metrics that matter—reduction in recurring customer-impacting incidents and ticket volume as the headline, with operational signals (recurring-problem count, MTTR, RCA compliance, and SLA adherence) as supporting measures.
* Run problem-review cadences, maintain and drive down a prioritized problem backlog, and track held known errors so workarounds do not quietly become permanent technical debt.
* Identify automation and process-improvement opportunities and program-manage their delivery to reduce manual, repetitive work.
* Maintain authoritative documentation and a known-error knowledge base in Confluence, and provide clear, executive-level status, risks, and escalations.

**Required Qualifications**

* 10-12 years of experience in technical program management, security or IT operations, data and analytics, or service/problem management; Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
* Proven ability to manage cross-functional programs and drive outcomes across multiple teams without direct authority.
* Hands-on data analysis: able to query operational and security data using KQL (Microsoft Sentinel/Defender) and SQL, and to build reports and dashboards (e.g., Power BI, Jira) that surface trends and quantify impact.
* Working understanding of data integrations—connectors, APIs, and ingestion pipelines—and how security telemetry reaches a SIEM or analytics platform (e.g., Microsoft Sentinel, Microsoft Defender).
* Solid grounding in problem management and root cause analysis, aligned to ITIL (Problem, Incident, and Service Management).
* Familiarity (conceptual, not hands-on delivery) with the security domains Armor operates: vulnerability management (Qualys/VMDR), endpoint and EDR (Microsoft Defender), and cloud and identity (Azure, Okta/Entra).
* Ability to read incident and ticket data and translate it into prioritized, measurable action.
* Excellent communication and stakeholder management in English, including executive-level reporting and clear RCAs and resolution frameworks.
* Proficiency with Jira and Confluence.
* Strategic, systemic thinker with a bias for repeatable, automation-assisted solutions over one-off fixes.
* Self-directed, taking strategic direction and prioritization from the Head of Support.

****Alignment to Armor Core Values****

* COMMITMENT TO GROWTH
* INTEGRITY ALWAYS
* EMPATHY IN ACTION
* IMMEDIATE IMPACT
* FOLLOW-THROUGH

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Depth in KQL/Kusto, Power BI, or Power Automate, or exposure to data engineering and pipeline troubleshooting.
* Experience building or troubleshooting API-based integrations and data connectors.
* PMP, ITIL v4, or Microsoft security/Azure certifications.
* Experience in a cybersecurity or managed-security services (MSSP) environment.

title: PPC Marketing Specialist (Remote)
description:
**Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked.**
That is the whole job.
  
  
Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business.
  
  
So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face.
  
  
At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero.
  
  
You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end.
  
  
Here is what "end to end" actually means.
  
  
**You are the account manager. We do not have any.**
You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.
  
  
**You own the whole funnel, not the campaign.**
Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.
  
  
**You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it.**
We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number.
  
  
**You can live anywhere.**
We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output.
  
  
If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we will both know it fast.
  
  
If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.
  
  
**Requirements**
**What the job looks like**

* Own a set of DTC accounts as the strategist, the buyer, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $5k/mo to well into six figures a month
* Own the client relationship. There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you are the one who answers when something is not working
* Audit before you touch anything. Every account we take over gets a real review first: campaign and ad group structure, keywords versus search terms, negatives, bidding strategy per campaign type, impression share, feed health, landing pages, audiences, and conversion tracking. Then a Loom walking the client through what you found. That Loom is how we sell and it is how we keep people
* Run brand and non brand as different businesses. Brand is mostly assisted conversion and it usually belongs on target impression share, not target CPA. Non brand is where the growth is and where the waste is. Report them separately or you are reporting nothing
* Know what PMax is actually doing. The most common mistake we see is optimizing PMax against an incremental CAC when half the volume inside it is branded. If you cannot separate those two, you cannot set a target
* Keep Google's automation on a leash. Auto applied recommendations, auto applied assets, and auto created sitelinks have cost our clients real money. We audit for them on a schedule
* Own the feed. Merchant Center hygiene, product titles, disapprovals, promotions, and what the feed does to Shopping and PMax delivery
* Own the tracking. GA4, GTM, Shopify goal imports versus a raw Google Ads tag, enhanced conversions, offline conversion imports for the lead gen accounts. When the numbers do not reconcile, you are the one who finds out why
* Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it. Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout, tracking. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team
* Build the things the account needs. Landing pages, scripts, reporting, whatever removes the constraint. We are heavy AI users and we expect you to build, not just prompt

**You are a fit if**

* You have done this with real money. Hands on Google Ads at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them. Shopping and PMax specifically, not just search
* You are fluent in the whole stack, not one campaign type. Search, Shopping, PMax, Demand Gen, YouTube, Merchant Center, GA4, GTM. Bing is a nice to have
* You are AI native, and you build. This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude or equivalent as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it
* You can communicate your ideas in English at a native or near native level. You will be in front of clients constantly. You need to explain your thinking clearly, sell an idea on its merits, push back when a client is about to force the account into mediocrity, and raise a problem before it becomes a fire. This matters as much as anything else on this list
* You are skeptical of your own numbers. You would rather run the holdout than protect the dashboard
* You can work US Eastern business hours for client calls. Where you live is up to you
* Bonus: you have built or operated your own Shopify store, or you have run Meta at spend too

**You are not a fit if**

* "That was not my role" is in your vocabulary. It is the fastest way to end an interview here. If the feed was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the feed
* You want to be told what to do this week
* You need a ticketing system to know what matters
* You quote blended ROAS as if it settles the question

**Benefits**
**Why this role is exciting**
This is not a maintenance job. You would have real influence over how we run Google across the agency.
  
  
You will work on real brands with real budgets. We test aggressively. We learn quickly. We build frameworks that scale.
  
  
You get trust on day one. You get a lot of autonomy. Some people thrive with it. You will get feedback fast either way, and if you make it through the first 30 days you will probably be here for a long time. Our retention on this team is very good and that is not an accident.
  
  
You will grow into senior strategy. We want people who want more responsibility. If you perform, you will grow.

* Revenue and profitability by product line
* Market share growth vs. competitors

* Roadmap execution (on-time, in-scope delivery)
* Customer satisfaction and product adoption
